<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Evidence and belief</p><h1>Bayesian Modeling for Psychologists, Part 1</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>11 Feb 2024</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>Bayesian modeling is a way to make uncertainty part of the model instead of a footnote after the model. This first article is a practical introduction for psychologists who want to update their statistical toolkit.</p><h2>The question</h2><p>What does it mean to update a belief with data, when the data are noisy and the prior is not optional?</p><h2>The workflow</h2><p>Start with a generative story. Write down the likelihood. Choose a prior that can be explained. Fit the model. Then inspect the posterior rather than stopping at a single summary.</p><pre><code>posterior ∝ likelihood × prior</code></pre><p>The original article remains a technical walk-through with its code and equations preserved in the archive source.</p></article></main>
